Update: Fort Hare

By: Sipha Kema | Delivery

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
A major breakthrough in the University of Fort Hare assasinations that left the country stunned...

Unique Selling Point:
The University of Fort Hare story is developing...
After month of investigation five suspects linked to the murder of the University of Fort Hare’s Vice-Chancellor's bodyguard and the institution's fleet manager and the attempted murder of the some of the university's staff were arrested over the Easter weekend.

Three of the five suspects are linked to the university - two are former employees and one a former student and member of the SRC.

We have a one on one with Fort Hare University's Vice-Chancellor following the five accused first court appearance.

Summary:
Five suspects linked to the murder of the University of Fort Hare’s Vice-Chancellor's bodyguard and the attempted murder of the Vice-Chancellor and the members of the Executive body at the university appeared before the Alice Magistrates Court on Tuesday.

Fort Hare University has been rocked by scandals of corruption and violence over the past few years resulting in two murders and shootings outside the residence of some employees.
Police investigations have lead to five suspects arrested in connection to the murder of two employees at the University of Fort Hare.
In May 2022, Fleet Manager Peet Roets was gunned down in Gonubie, East London on his way home. The recent murder of Professor Sakhela Buhlungu’s bodyguard, Mboneli Vesele this January - rocked the entire country. It's believed the bullet was meant for the University’s Vice-Chancellor.

A series of corruption was uncovered following Vesele's murder. which we exposed.
We speak with Vice-Chancellor Professor Sakhela Buhlungu and he talks to us about the arrests.


Further information:
The one on one interview with the University of Fort Hare's Vice-Chancellor, Professor Sakhela Buhlungu, he speaks about the disappointment in finding three of the suspects are linked to the university - Bongani Peter and Wanini Khuza were trusted employees in the transport department. Buhlungu says this was also no surprise.

The Vice-Chancellor says we can expect big names and politicians on the Police Minister Bheki Cele's upcoming arrests.

In January this year, Mboneli Vesele, the man tasked with guarding Fort Hare University’s Vice Chancellor, was assassinated. It followed the gunning down of the university’s Fleet Manager, Petrus Roets, a year earlier.

VO: Our investigation revealed damning evidence of fraud and corruption involving high-placed politicians and university staff. Vice Chancellor, Professor Sakela Buhlungu, couldn’t hide his frustration.

Timecode:

“They were in the process of laundering that registration into doctoral degrees.”

Whatsapp Message Statement

Cell Phone Footage from Alice Court

[CELLPHONE FOOTAGE]
VO: Now, months later, a breakthrough:

police have arrested five suspects linked to the two murders and the attempted murders of several of the university’s staff.

Clip name: 20230411_112719 [CELLPHONE FOOTAGE]
UPSOUND: FANNIE MASEMOLA; NATIONAL POLICE COMMISSIONER
1:07 – 1:17
“Two of the suspects are from KwaZulu-Natal and the rest of the three are from here at Eastern Cape. We arrested them over the long weekend.”
6 CELLPHONE FOOTAGE
Visuals of courtroom and outside the courtroom with Cele, Maemola and Buhlungu [CELLPHONE FOOTAGE]
VO: In a sinister twist, it’s alleged the mastermind of the murders is a senior University employee, Bongani Peter. Also among those arrested are the Chancelor’s driver, and a former member of the SRC turned service provider. The court ruled that they’re faces could not be identified.
7 CELLPHONE FOOTAGE
Interview with Professor Sakhela Buhlungu [CELLPHONE FOOTAGE]
UPSOUND: PROFESSOR SAKHELA BUHLUNGU; UFH VICE-CHANCELLOR
0:42 – 0:48
“I don’t think we had a sense of the extent or the magnitude of the involvement by internal people.”


8 Visuals of Prof Buhlungu VO: Professor Buhlungu says he had his suspicions about Peter.
9 CELLPHONE FOOTAGE
Interview with Professor Sakhela Buhlungu [CELLPHONE FOOTAGE]
UPSOUND: PROFESSOR SAKHELA BUHLUNGU; UFH VICE-CHANCELLOR
1:41 – 2:02
“We always knew he was up to something but not to this extent…Mr Peter was also responsible for all vehicle trackers. So, theoretically he could track my vehicle back and forth. He could track any car.”
10 CELLPHONE FOOTAGE
Interview with Professor Sakhela Buhlungu [CELLPHONE FOOTAGE]
UPSOUND: PROFESSOR SAKHELA BUHLUNGU; UFH VICE-CHANCELLOR
2:14 – 2:22
Just after Mr Roets was killed in May last year – we did get information that Mr Peter had threatened Mr Roets.
11 CELLPHONE FOOTAGE


Inside Court


Visuals of outside court [CELLPHONE FOOTAGE]
VO: The University’s own investigators allege
Peter was attempting to defraud Fort Hare through its transport department and Roets was getting in his way.

Other arrests are likely to follow.


12 CELLPHONE FOOTAGE
Interview with Professor Sakhela Buhlungu [CELLPHONE FOOTAGE]
UPSOUND: PROFESSOR SAKHELA BUHLUNGU; UFH VICE-CHANCELLOR
7:44 – 7:54
“South Africa is going to be shocked, South Africa is going to be shocked and there’s no doubt about that one. As I’ve said before, you are going to see some big names there.


13
VO: Despite the arrests and additional security, Professor Buhlungu remains anxious.
14 CELLPHONE FOOTAGE
Interview with Professor Sakhela Buhlungu [CELLPHONE FOOTAGE]
UPSOUND: PROFESSOR SAKHELA BUHLUNGU; UFH VICE-CHANCELLOR
11:32
“Take today, there’s a car that’s doing the rounds around the house and stopped by three times outside my gate. Today, today.


15
With more arrests on the horizon, the University of Fort Hare story is far from over…
